summary: sitecard CLI exposes local shell over public tunnel with no-auth default
details: The `sitecard` CLI starts an AsyncSSH gateway (gateway.py) whose TokenSSHServer.begin_auth returns False when config.accept is set, admitting SSH clients without credentials, and pipes SSH channel bytes into a child process's stdin/PTY. ingress.py bridges the local gateway port to a public tunnel host (srv.us, uptermd.upterm.dev, or cloudflared), and fresh sessions default to `--public-access`, meaning newly started sessions accept any inbound client with no authentication. The capability is disclosed as the package's advertised purpose (README describes exposing temporary SSH access), and the channel comes up only when the user explicitly runs the `sitecard start` subcommand — no install-time, import-time, or boot-persistence execution is present. The tunnel endpoints are hardcoded but user-configurable. The result is that any peer who learns the tunnel URL of a default-configured session can obtain interactive shell execution on the host running the CLI.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
